Latent transition analysis

lta.Rd

Fits a latent transition model to categorical or continuous indicators measured at two or more waves: one latent class (profile) variable per wave, with first-order (Markov) transitions between consecutive waves.

Usage

lta(
  data,
  waves,
  K,
  invariance = "full",
  transitions = "timevarying",
  starts = c(100, 20),
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariates_on = "all",
  interaction = FALSE,
  distal = NULL,
  distal_categorical = NULL,
  distal_wave = NULL,
  distal_variances = "equal",
  weights = NULL,
  indicators = NULL,
  variances = "equal",
  covariances = "zero",
  start = NULL,
  optseed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix (one row per respondent). Indicators may be factors, characters, logicals, labelled vectors or numeric category codes; NA marks a missing response.

waves

A list with the indicator columns of each wave, in the same item order, e.g. list(a1:a6, b1:b6, c1:c6) (tidyselect inside list()), list(1:6, 7:12, 13:18), or a list of character vectors. At least two waves.

K

Number of classes (a positive whole number).

invariance

"full" (measurement parameters equal across waves, default) or "none"; for continuous indicators also partial invariance (see Details): a vector of items, a named list item = waves, or list(means = , variances = ).

transitions

"timevarying" (default) or "stationary".

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

cluster

Optional primary sampling units (PSUs) of a complex survey design (Mplus CLUSTER with TYPE = COMPLEX): one column of data (e.g. psu) or a vector with one value per row. Standard errors, the MLR scaling correction factor and the tests built on them (compare_models(), Wald tests of r3step(), bch(), dcat()) are then design-based: computed from PSU totals of the weighted scores. Estimates and the log-likelihood do not change. blrt() is not available (as in Mplus). Analysed rows may not have a missing value.

strata

Optional strata of the design (Mplus STRATIFICATION): one column of data or a vector. PSUs are nested in strata (equal cluster codes in different strata are different PSUs); without cluster every row is its own PSU. A stratum with a single PSU is kept, as in Mplus.

covariates

Covariates of the latent classes (one-step; numeric columns, dummy-code factors): a selection such as c(female, ses) for time-invariant covariates used at every wave, or list(x_1, x_2, x_3) with one selection per wave for time-varying covariates (wave t's columns enter the initial class at wave 1 and the transition into wave t). Mplus c1 ON x; c2 ON c1 x; .... Rows with a missing covariate are deleted (as in Mplus).

covariates_on

"all" (initial classes and transitions, default), "initial" (c1 ON x only) or "transitions".

interaction

TRUE: covariate effects on the transitions differ by the class at the previous wave (Mplus c2 ON x inside MODEL c1:, User's Guide Ex. 8.14).

distal

Distal outcomes of the class at distal_wave (default: last wave), estimated jointly with the LTA (one step): numeric columns, normal within class (class-specific means).

distal_categorical

The columns of distal that are categorical (class-specific probabilities).

distal_wave

Wave whose class the distal outcomes depend on (default: last).

distal_variances

"equal" (default) or "varying" within-class variances of continuous distal outcomes.

weights

Sampling weights: a column of data (e.g. wt) or a numeric vector with one value per row, rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows (Mplus WEIGHT); robust standard errors use the squared weights.

indicators

"categorical", "continuous", or NULL (default: continuous when every indicator is numeric with more than ten distinct values, else categorical).

variances

Continuous indicators: within-class variances "equal" across classes (default) or "varying".

covariances

Continuous indicators: "zero" (local independence, default), "equal" (one full covariance matrix, with variances = "equal") or "varying" (with variances = "varying").

start

Optional start values: a fitted latentmix model of the same type and number of classes (for example a fit to other data, or with fewer random starts). EM then runs from its estimates only, without random starts (Mplus user starting values with STARTS = 0; the analogue of OUTPUT: SVALUES).

optseed

Optional start number: rerun only that random start (stage 1 and stage 2), the analogue of Mplus OPTSEED; see refit_start().

Value

An object of class latentmix (see lca()) with info$kind == "LTA", info$classprobs a class-by-wave matrix, and the extra components waves (column positions per wave) and wave_names (column names per wave).

Details

The same items must be measured at every wave, listed in the same order in each element of waves. With invariance = "full" (the usual LTA) the item-response probabilities are equal across waves, so classes have the same meaning at every wave; with "none" they are estimated separately at each wave. transitions = "timevarying" (Mplus default) estimates one transition matrix per pair of consecutive waves, "stationary" a single matrix shared by all pairs.

With indicators = "continuous" (chosen automatically when every indicator is numeric with more than ten distinct values) every wave has a latent profile model with class-specific means; variances and covariances set the within-class (co)variances as in lpa(). Indicators are standardised with one centre and scale per item position, pooled over the waves; results are reported on the raw scale. Measurement invariance can then be partial, wave 1 being the reference: invariance = c("stress_1", "lonely_1") (or item positions c(3, 4)) frees the means of those items at every later wave; invariance = list(stress_1 = 2, lonely_1 = 2) frees them at the listed waves only; invariance = list(means = ..., variances = ...) frees means and variances separately (each element in either form, or "full"/"none"; variances only with covariances = "zero"). Item names may be given for any wave. Use profilemeans(), profilevariances() and profilecovariances() with wave.

Missing items and whole missing waves are handled by full-information maximum likelihood; rows with no observed indicator at any wave are not analysed. The R interface supports categorical and continuous indicators, with optional sampling weights. With covariates the initial classes follow a multinomial logit on the covariates and every transition matrix a multinomial logit on the previous class and the covariates (estimated in one step with the measurement model); parameters() and coeftable() give the coefficients with robust standard errors in the Mplus parameterisation, and transitions() with at the transition probabilities at given covariate values. For three-step alternatives that keep the measurement model fixed see lta3step(), r3step() (wave) and bch() (wave, waves). cluster and strata make the standard errors, the scaling factor and compare_models() design-based. Test measurement invariance across waves with compare_models() ("full" against "none").

References

Collins, L. M., & Lanza, S. T. (2010). Latent Class and Latent Transition Analysis: With Applications in the Social, Behavioral, and Health Sciences. Wiley.

See also

transitions(), itemprobs() (wave argument), posterior(), compare_models().

Examples

data(substance)
# \donttest{
# past-30-day alcohol, binge drinking, cigarette and cannabis use in grades 8, 10, 12:
# how do students move between substance-use statuses?
t3 <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
t3
#> ━━ Latent transition analysis ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   3 classes × 3 waves, n = 1500; measurement invariant across waves; time-specific transitions
#>   Random starts: 100 / 20; best LL replicated 20 times
#> 
#> ── Fit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#>   Free parameters            26      BIC                   13214.315
#>   Observations             1500      Sample-size adj. BIC  13131.720
#>   Best LL replicated    20 / 20      Entropy                   0.722
#> 
#> ── Class proportions by wave ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            Wave 1  Wave 2  Wave 3

#>   alc_1 = 0          0.938    0.139    0.059
#>   alc_1 = 1          0.062    0.861    0.941

#>   binge_1 = 1        0.014    0.339    0.710
#>   cig_1 = 0          0.982    0.878    0.451
#>   cig_1 = 1          0.018    0.122    0.549
#>   mj_1 = 0           0.990    0.894    0.436
#>   mj_1 = 1           0.010    0.106    0.564
#> 
#> ── Transitions, wave 1 → 2 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            to 1   to 2   to 3

#> ── Transitions, wave 2 → 3 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#>   from 1  0.670  0.217  0.112

#>   summary() for standard errors · lm_table() to export · classify() for posteriors
transitions(t3)   # rows = from, columns = to; non-users mostly stay non-users
#> [[1]]
#>         to
#> from           class1    class2     class3
#>   class1 6.887848e-01 0.2436745 0.06754074
#>   class2 1.030446e-01 0.7269494 0.17000598
#>   class3 6.808015e-16 0.1686199 0.83138015
#> 
#> [[2]]
#>         to
#> from        class1    class2    class3

#>   class2 0.0665107 0.7368759 0.1966134
#>   class3 0.0162164 0.1291587 0.8546249
#> 
# measurement invariance over time (true here): compare with wave-specific items
t3_free <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3,
               invariance = "none")
compare_models(t3, t3_free)   # large p: invariant item probabilities are adequate
#> ━━ Nested model comparison ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
#>   Model               LL  Par.  Scaling
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
#>   M0: t3       -6512.086    26   1.0104
#>   M1: t3_free  -6505.781    50   1.0581
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Difference tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Test                          Chi-square  df      p

#>   Likelihood ratio (naive, ML)      12.609  24  0.972
#>   Satorra-Bentler scaled (MLR)      11.362  24  0.986
#>   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Scaling correction of the difference cd = 1.1098
#>   ΔAIC = 35.391, ΔBIC = 162.908, ΔsaBIC = 86.667 (M1 - M0)

# continuous indicators: sleep, activity, stress and loneliness of 700 adults in 2019,
# 2020 and 2021; stress and loneliness rose in every profile in 2020 (generated +1.5, +1.0)
data(wellbeing_panel)
wb <- list(sleep_1:lonely_1, sleep_2:lonely_2, sleep_3:lonely_3)
#> Error: object 'sleep_1' not found
c_full <- lta(wellbeing_panel, waves = wb, K = 3, indicators = "continuous")
#> Error: object 'wb' not found
c_part <- lta(wellbeing_panel, waves = wb, K = 3, indicators = "continuous",
              invariance = list(stress_1 = 2, lonely_1 = 2))   # free in 2020 only
#> Error: object 'wb' not found
compare_models(c_full, c_part)        # partial invariance fits better
#> Error: object 'c_full' not found
round(profilemeans(c_part, wave = 2) - profilemeans(c_part, wave = 1), 2)
#> Error: object 'c_part' not found
